extracted.intended_audience: readers of periodical essays; aspiring essayists and writers of character sketches
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for composing short moralizing character sketches and descriptive periodical essays that reveal character through anecdote, dress, setting, and reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for odd and uncommon characters
rubrics_metrics.description: “Odd and uncommon Characters are the Game that I look for, and most delight in.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value novelty and individuality in characterization; seek out peculiar, distinctive figures (e.g., Will Wimble) whose small habits and humours provide sustained interest and material for anecdote. Use such characters as the central thread of a short essay to engage readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dress to indicate character and era
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is worth while to consider the Force of Dress; and how the Persons of one Age differ from those of another, merely by that only.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use costume and clothing details to signal social rank, period, temperament, and to produce visual comedy or dignity (examples: jetting coat and small bonnet making someone look taller/broader; petticoat vs modern gathered waist). Dress can be a shorthand to position a character in society and history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use setting and sensory detail to create atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of the walk of aged elms, rooks and crows, ruins, echoes, and dusk that make a scene 'proper' for a ghost to appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build mood through concrete sensory details (sight, sound, echoes, bird-calls, ruins) and by juxtaposing setting elements (ivy-covered ruins, churchyard marks, elms). These particulars create a felt atmosphere which can be used either to produce suspense or to be later explained/demystified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain or demystify uncanny effects by appeal to psychology/theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to Locke's 'association of ideas' to explain why darkness becomes connected to goblins and spirits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying supernatural or uncanny impressions, authors can either lean into mystery or provide rational/psychological accounts that show how fears arise (e.g., associative learning). Citing or invoking a theory can deepen the essay's reflective move from sensation to explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral reflection and social critique woven into portraiture
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrator moves from an account of Will Wimble's busy harmless industry to a reflection on how younger sons disdain trade, producing 'Pride and Beggary'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a character vignette as the springboard for broader moral or social commentary. Let an anecdote prompt reflection about customs, class, or national character—this gives color while advancing an argumentative or didactic point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compress biography via portrait anecdotes and emblematic details
rubrics_metrics.description: Portrait-descriptions that combine costume, a few pointed anecdotes, and emblematic objects (viol, broken lance) to sum up an ancestor's qualities and life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sketching a life in brief, select telling incidents and emblematic props to imply longer histories (e.g., a broken lance suggests martial prowess; a hanging viol suggests peaceful arts). Short anecdotes can stand in for full biography to produce wit and judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance whimsy and good sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixture of 'the Whim of narrowly escaping' with 'good Sense' produces delight in Sir Roger's simplicity and wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine playful, whimsical anecdote or oddity with sober moral observation to create both amusement and weight. The interplay of humour and seriousness is a stylistic strength in the periodical essay—neither should wholly dominate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict small social rituals to reveal power relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Details such as giving hassocks and prayer books, walking down between rows of tenants, or waking a nodding parishioner characterize Sir Roger's stewardship and local authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show rather than state social order: render minor public rituals (church behaviour, gifts, gestures) that demonstrate a character's influence, obligations, and relationships within a community. Such particulars reveal social texture and moral authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concrete objects and handicrafts to reveal temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Will Wimble's may-flies, angle-rods, tulip-root, knitted garters, and shuttlecocks mark him as inventive, officious, and pleasingly industrious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List small belongings, handmade items, or habitual actions to evoke a character's temperament, skills, and social role. Domestic and artisanal details create intimacy and make characterization credible and vivid.
